deep.reconstruction:
The page continues a tabulation of a monotone angular function f(x). It runs from x = 6.550 to 6.850 in steps of h = 0.002 and continues pp. 193 and 195. The layout is two blocks of 50 lines, each repeated in three column-groups: 6.550–6.650, 6.650–6.750 and 6.750–6.850. The last line of each block is copied as the first line of the next.

Column 1 is the argument x.

Column 2 is f(x) in degrees, minutes and seconds, given to 1e-5 arcsecond. When the minute or degree changes, the leading part is written in full, e.g. 138°11'32.63765" at 6.550 and 147°41'13.07864" at 6.850.

Column 3 is the first difference in arcseconds: Δ1(x) = f(x+h) − f(x). For example, at 6.552: 20'21.15089" − 15'57.17391" = 263.97698".

Column 4 is the second difference in units of 1e-5", written beside the lower argument: Δ2(x) = Δ1(x−h) − Δ1(x) > 0. For example, at 6.552: 264.53626 − 263.97698 = 0.55928 → 55928. The first entry, 56081 at 6.550, implies Δ1(6.548) = 265.09707" on the preceding (unseen) part of the table.

The columns serve as a running check. Within each block the values were evidently built by accumulating differences (f(x+h) = f(x) + Δ1(x), Δ1(x+h) = Δ1(x) − Δ2(x+h)). The smoothness of Δ2, whose third differences run about −150 to −95 units, guards the twelve-figure values.

Behaviour of the function:
- The slope df/dx falls from about 0.641 rad/unit at 6.55 to about 0.473 at 6.85.
- f(x) rises towards 180°. π − f falls from 0.730 to 0.564 rad, roughly like e^{−0.86x}.
- Equivalently, f'' / f' ≈ −1.06 → −0.97.

I could not identify the function. Simple candidates fail the slope and curvature data: Gudermannian-type f' ∝ sin f, f' ∝ 1+cos f, the Kepler mean-to-eccentric or mean-to-true anomaly maps, and the Jacobi amplitude. Its purpose within the 'Lagrange 1816' material is therefore not determinable from this page alone (my statement).
errors: Rows 6.766–6.770 are internally inconsistent as transcribed. With f(6.768) = 145°22'9.72523", the first differences are 212.02324 and 211.60349, giving second differences 42112, 41975, 41897 instead of the smooth 42102, 41995, 41887 written in column 4. The smooth Δ2 column and Δ1(6.770) = 211.18452 force Δ1(6.766) = 212.02334 and f(6.768) = 145°22'9.72533". So the values should end ...72533, 212.02334 and 211.60339. The image shows visible overwriting at exactly these places ('23', '24', '39', '95'), so Gauss very likely caught and corrected this himself; the transcription may preserve the pre-correction digits.

Row 6.792: Δ1 is written 206.64696, but 146°7'28.20189" − 146°4'1.55491" = 206.64698". The values 206.64698 would give second differences 40727 and 40623, smoother than the written 40729 and 40621 (third differences −103, −104, −104). This is a 2-unit slip in the last place of the difference column, propagated into two Δ2 entries; the function values themselves appear right.
All other spot checks reproduce exactly, including all the heavily overwritten entries: 6.578 (53986), 6.628 (50466), 6.636 (13'0.88020"), 6.648 (49135), 6.656 (48615), 6.774–6.778 and 6.838–6.848.

results.what: High-precision (1e-5") table of an angular function f(x) at step 0.002, with first and second differences used as a running check / construction by summation of differences
results.usually_credited_to: Standard practice since Briggs and Newton; routine in 18th–19th c. table making

results.what: The specific function tabulated: a smooth increasing angle approaching 180°, with f' ≈ 0.64 → 0.47 rad per unit on [6.55, 6.85]
results.modern_name: unidentified (possibly an auxiliary angle connected with the 'Lagrange 1816' material)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely numerical auxiliary table with a standard difference check, of the kind Gauss produced in quantity. It shows his computational stamina and a self-corrected slip, but no new method or result. The underlying function is unidentified from this page.
